≺.justification: The reverse morphism describing the descent of the harmonic sum density towards zero.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of terms in the summation over the set A.

⊙.justification: An element x in A that recognizes its own position within the separation constraints.

∈.justification: The split into two mutually exclusive paths: the path of logarithmic convergence and the path of harmonic vanishing.

∋.justification: The reconstitution of the two branches into the single logical disjunction that constitutes the theorem's conclusion.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the limit of the harmonic sum over A is zero.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where the separation condition |(k*x)-y| >= 1 holds simultaneously for all pairs, maintaining the tension between density and sparsity.

◻.justification: The permanent record of the separation condition for a specific pair (x,y) and integer k.

Affirm the state where the logarithmic sum converges to a finite value.
Record the convergence of the logarithmic sum as a permanent fact.
Descend along the F-arm to evaluate the decay of the harmonic density.
Compose the terms of the harmonic sum 1/x over the intersection with [1, n].
Affirm the state where the limit of the harmonic sum is zero.
Record the vanishing density as a permanent fact.
Hold the separation condition |(k*x)-y| >= 1 active across both branches simultaneously.
Rejoin the T-arm (log convergence) and F-arm (harmonic vanishing) into the disjunctive conclusion.
Anchor the system in the proven dichotomy that one of the two states must hold.
